title: Functional characterization of PfHDDCP reveals a HotDog-domain acyl‑CoA thioesterase as a potential antimalarial drug target.
authors: Gupta, Pooja; Kaushik, Naveen Kumar; Goyal, Parveen; Dhir, Sunny; Pai, Somnath S; Sharma, Anil
one_liner_zh: 该文对疟原虫HotDog结构域硫酯酶进行生化表征和分子对接，虽涉及蛋白结构相关计算（对接），但核心是酶学实验与药物抑制，缺乏AI或物理模拟方法创新，与蛋白质结构计算课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thioesterases play a central role in maintaining acyl‑CoA homeostasis and lipid metabolic flux, processes that are critical for the intraerythrocytic development of Plasmodium falciparum. Plasmodium falciparum HotDog domain-containing protein [PfHDDCP (PF3D7_1135400; previously annotated as PF11_0364, XP_001348035.1)] has been computationally predicted to function as an acyl-CoA thioesterase, although experimental validation was lacking. Here, we present the first biochemical characterization of PfHDDCP and demonstrate its thioesterase activity. METHODS AND RESULTS: The PfHDDCP gene was cloned into the pRSET-A vector, expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3), purified under denaturing conditions, and refolded. Enzymatic assays revealed no detectable protease activity but demonstrated robust thioesterase activity toward acetyl-CoA using a DTNB-based colorimetric assay. Kinetic analysis yielded a Km of 11.68 microM and a Vmax of 16.28 x 10(-)(5) micromol/min, with substrate inhibition at elevated acetyl-CoA concentrations. PfHDDCP showed maximal catalytic activity at pH 8.0 and 37  degrees C and retained substantial activity at 40-42  degrees C. Fe(2)(+) and Ca(2)(+) had no significant effect on activity, whereas Mg(2)(+) markedly reduced activity at the higher concentrations tested. Molecular docking predicted favorable heme binding, but neither spectroscopy nor native PAGE supported stable heme association in vitro. Artemisinin derivatives showed favorable predicted interactions with PfHDDCP and inhibited its thioesterase activity in vitro, whereas chloroquine had a substantially weaker effect. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings establish PfHDDCP as a functional HotDog domain-containing acyl-CoA thioesterase and support its potential involvement in parasite lipid metabolism. The inhibition observed with selected antimalarial compounds identifies PfHDDCP as a candidate for further investigation of drug-enzyme interactions. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not Applicable.
abstract_zh: 背景：硫酯酶 (thioesterases) 在维持酰基辅酶A (acyl-CoA) 稳态和脂质代谢流中发挥核心作用，这些过程对恶性疟原虫 (Plasmodium falciparum) 的红细胞内发育至关重要。恶性疟原虫含HotDog结构域蛋白 [PfHDDCP (PF3D7_1135400；此前注释为PF11_0364, XP_001348035.1)] 经计算预测具有酰基辅酶A硫酯酶功能，但缺乏实验验证。在此，我们首次对PfHDDCP进行生化表征并证明其硫酯酶活性。方法与结果：将PfHDDCP基因克隆至pRSET-A载体，在大肠杆菌 (Escherichia coli) BL21(DE3)中表达，在变性条件下纯化并复性。酶学实验未检测到蛋白酶活性，但通过基于DTNB的比色法证实其对乙酰辅酶A (acetyl-CoA) 具有强硫酯酶活性。动力学分析得出Km为11.68 microM，Vmax为16.28 x 10(-)(5) micromol/min，在乙酰辅酶A浓度升高时出现底物抑制。PfHDDCP在pH 8.0和37 摄氏度时表现出最大催化活性，并在40-42 摄氏度时保留显著活性。Fe(2)(+)和Ca(2)(+)对活性无显著影响，而Mg(2)(+)在测试的较高浓度下显著降低活性。分子对接 (molecular docking) 预测其与血红素 (heme) 结合良好，但光谱学和天然PAGE均不支持在体外形成稳定的血红素结合。青蒿素 (artemisinin) 衍生物与PfHDDCP预测具有良好相互作用，并在体外抑制其硫酯酶活性，而氯喹 (chloroquine) 的作用明显较弱。结论：总体而言，这些发现确立了PfHDDCP是一种功能性含HotDog结构域的酰基辅酶A硫酯酶，并支持其可能参与寄生虫脂质代谢。所选抗疟化合物观察到的抑制作用使PfHDDCP成为进一步研究药物-酶相互作用的候选靶点。临床试验编号：不适用。
